# Tool reference: Building Architect server (buildingarchitect)

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_tool_docs.py from the server's tools/list; do not edit by hand -->

47 tools. Every tool takes JSON arguments as described and returns compact JSON text, except `guide` (markdown) and the image tools (`view_image`, `project_image`, `rendered_image`, `texture_image`: a PNG; `render_building`: JSON text + a PNG). Failures are MCP tool errors (`isError: true`) whose text is JSON `{"error": ..., "hint": ...}`.

Kinds map to the MCP tool annotations each tool carries:

| kind | readOnlyHint | destructiveHint | idempotentHint | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| read | True | False | True | reads the Building Architect, changes nothing |
| set | False | False | True | sets a value (idempotent) |
| act | False | False | False | acts in the Building Architect |
| destructive | False | True | False | can discard something (the building being edited, the program) |

All tools have openWorldHint false (they act on the local game only).

## Server instructions

Sent to the client at initialization:

> Makes buildings for SimCity 3000 Unlimited. (1) Drives the game's Building Architect: create and edit buildings (blocks, roofs, paints, details, props), see them as images read from the program and its rendered output (no screenshots), render them for the game - start with bat_launch. (2) Photo to building, no Architect needed: photo_add, photo_view (measure the photo), then a model of 3D parts whose walls are drawn as authored facades, rendered by photo_model_render and written into the game's format by photo_model_export (higher quality); photo_buildings / photo_building_remove manage what is installed. Call guide() first (guide(topic='photo') for the photo route and its best practices).

Read it first.

## game_building_image

*read*

One of SimCity 3000's own buildings or landmarks as the game draws it, decoded from the game's sprite files (no screenshot) - the reference for scale, level of detail and style when designing a building: compare it with render_building at the same zoom. Returns its lot size and a picture of the chosen rotation (or all four). Covers the default (North American) building style.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | The building's name as the game calls it (e.g. "Empire State Building", "Hospital", "Mayor's House"), a unique part of it, or its occupant id (e.g. "0x252C"). |
| `zoom` | integer | `5` | 1 (smallest) .. 5 (largest; the game draws zoom 5 as zoom 4 doubled, as it does for user buildings). |
| `rotation` | integer | `-1` | 0..3, or -1 for all four side by side. |

## new_building

*destructive*

Start a new building in the Building Architect (its New Building button and Tile Size dialog). The building being edited is replaced; unsaved changes to it are lost (save_building first). The new lot has a ground layer at z = 0; build from z = 1 up.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | integer | `1` | Lot size in city tiles a side: 1..5 (1x1 = 8 x 8 cells and 28 cells high; 2x2 16 x 16 x 64; 3x3 24 x 24 x 108; 4x4 32 x 32 x 144; 5x5 40 x 40 x 80). |
| `name` | string | `'New Building'` | Building name (shown in SimCity's Query). |
| `architect` | string | `''` | Architect name. |
| `description` | string | `''` | Description text. |
| `building_type` | string | `'residential'` | residential \| commercial \| industrial \| police_station \| jail \| fire_station \| hospital \| school \| college \| library \| museum \| historic_statue \| mayors_house \| city_hall \| performing_arts_center \| other. |

## shapes

*read*

The 16 block shapes (id, description, and what each face slot is at rotation 0: top, bottom, a side direction, or a sloped face and the way it faces) and the conventions: cells are (x, y, z) with z up, 8 cells per city tile; a shape's rotation 0..3 turns it 90 degrees counter-clockwise (x right, y up). A cube's slots are 0 top, 1 -x, 2 -y, 3 +x, 4 +y, 5 bottom (at rotation 0). The default camera looks from the +x, +y side, so top, +x and +y faces face the viewer. Paint tools accept direction names, so slot numbers are rarely needed.

No parameters.

## blocks

*read*

The blocks of the building being edited: position (x, y, z), shape, rotation and the paint / detail of each painted face slot; for shapes other than cubes also "slots": what each slot is (top, a side direction, a sloped face...).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `z_min` | integer | `1` | Lowest z to list. |
| `z_max` | integer | `1000` | Highest z to list. |
| `include_ground` | boolean | `false` | Also list the ground layer (z = 0). |

## place_blocks

*act*

Place blocks with the Building Architect's own SetBlock (replacing what is in those cells), each {"x": .., "y": .., "z": .., "shape": 0..15 (default 0 = cube), "rotation": 0..3}. z starts at 1 (0 is the ground). Returns the building's block count.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blocks` | array of object | required | The blocks to place. |

## fill_box

*act*

Fill a box of cells (both corners included) with one block shape, e.g. the body of a building.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x0` | integer | required | First corner x. |
| `y0` | integer | required | First corner y. |
| `z0` | integer | required | First corner z (1 = on the ground). |
| `x1` | integer | required | Opposite corner x. |
| `y1` | integer | required | Opposite corner y. |
| `z1` | integer | required | Opposite corner z. |
| `shape` | integer | `0` | Block shape 0..15 (shapes lists them; 0 = cube). |
| `rotation` | integer | `0` | 0..3. |

## roof

*act*

Build a roof from one or more rectangles, with the right block shape in every cell: slopes, hip corners, ridges and the valleys where roofs meet (the parts are combined by taking the highest surface, so a front gable crossing a hip roof gets proper valleys). Each part {"x0", "y0", "x1", "y1", "style", optional "pitch", "z", "max_height"}: style hip (slopes on all four sides), pyramid, gable_y (ridge along y, gable ends facing +y and -y), gable_x (ridge along x), shed_+x / shed_-x / shed_+y / shed_-y (one slope rising towards that side) or flat; max_height cuts the roof off flat at that many cells (a roof deck). Even widths give a sharp ridge; odd widths a flat ridge one cell wide. Optionally paints it: roof_texture on the slopes and tops, gable_texture on the vertical gable ends.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parts` | array of object | required | The roof rectangles (cells, both corners included), e.g. [{"x0": 3, "y0": 2, "x1": 12, "y1": 10, "style": "hip", "max_height": 3}, {"x0": 5, "y0": 6, "x1": 10, "y1": 10, "style": "gable_y"}]. |
| `z` | integer | required | Level of the lowest roof cells (the cell level just above the top of the walls). |
| `pitch` | number | `1.0` | 1 = 45 degrees (one cell up per cell in), 0.5 = 26.6 degrees; a part's own "pitch" overrides it. |
| `roof_texture` | string | `''` | Paint for the slopes and flat tops (library kind=roofs or any paint); empty to leave them. |
| `gable_texture` | string | `''` | Paint for the vertical gable-end faces (walls, shingles...); empty to leave them. |

*read*

## create_texture

*act*

Make a new paint texture or detail (decal) of your own and add it to the Architect's library, as its Apps\BACustom folders allow: a paint is saved as BACustom\Paints\<name>.bmp, a detail as BACustom\Details\<name>.tga (transparent parts let the paint show through). Each side must be a multiple of 16 px (16 px = one block face; up to 256). Give the picture as a file, as base64, or as pixel rows: one string per row, one palette character per pixel, e.g. rows ["aab", "abb"] with palette {"a": "#8a3b2a", "b": "200,200,200", ".": "transparent"}, enlarged by scale. Then use the name in paint_faces / fill_paint / detail_faces.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Name for the new texture (letters, digits, spaces, - and _), used as its library name. |
| `kind` | string | `'paint'` | paint \| detail. |
| `image_path` | string | `''` | A picture file (PNG, BMP, TGA, JPG...). |
| `image_base64` | string | `''` | A picture as base64 (or a data: URL). |
| `rows` | array of string or null | `null` | Pixel rows (all the same length) using palette characters. |
| `palette` | object or null | `null` | For rows: character -> colour ("#rrggbb", "r,g,b" or "transparent"). |
| `scale` | integer | `1` | Enlarge rows / the picture this many times (1..16), e.g. 16 x 16 rows with scale 2 -> 32 x 32 px. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | `false` | Replace a texture of that name made earlier in BACustom. |

## prop_template

*read*

Drawing guide for a new prop's four views (create_prop): four square bitmaps side by side (views 0..3), each showing the prop's box of cells exactly where the Architect places a prop picture - 2:1 isometric, one cell 32 px wide and 16 px deep, one storey 16 px high, the middle cell (index (n-1)//2 on each axis) centred, pink (255, 0, 255) = empty. The bitmap is the smallest of 32, 64, 128 or 256 px that fits, as the stock props use (a 1x1x1 prop is 32 px, a 1x1x13 antenna 256 px). Views 1 and 3 see the footprint turned. Draw the prop inside the box in each view, at this size.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | integer | required | Cells along x (1..7). |
| `depth` | integer | required | Cells along y (1..7). |
| `height` | integer | required | Cells high (1..14; it must fit a 256 px bitmap). |

## create_prop

*act*

Make a new prop of your own (as the Architect's BACustom\Props folder allows): four square view pictures (one per camera rotation, at the size and layout prop_template shows - 32, 64, 128 or 256 px; transparent or pink = empty) saved as BMPs with the .met file that tells the Architect the prop's size. Then place it with place_props(prop=name).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Prop name (letters, digits, spaces, - and _). |
| `width` | integer | required | Cells along x (1..7). |
| `depth` | integer | required | Cells along y (1..7). |
| `height` | integer | required | Cells high (1..28). |
| `views` | array of string or null | `null` | The four views as base64 pictures (or data: URLs), view 0 first. |
| `view_paths` | array of string or null | `null` | Or the four views as picture files. |
| `view_rows` | array of array of string or null | `null` | Or the four views as pixel rows with palette (each size / scale rows of size / scale characters). |
| `palette` | object or null | `null` | For view_rows: character -> colour ("#rrggbb", "r,g,b" or "transparent"). |
| `scale` | integer | `1` | Enlarge view_rows this many times (1..16). |
| `overwrite` | boolean | `false` | Replace a prop of that name made earlier in BACustom. |

## paint_faces

*act*

Paint block faces with textures, laid out continuously as the Architect's Paintbrush does (each 16x16 pixel cell of a texture covers one block face). Each face: {"x", "y", "z", "face", "texture": name from library (walls, roofs, ground, colors such as "color 162,161,201", custom), optional "u" / "v" to pick the texture cell yourself}; "texture": "" clears the paint. "face" is a direction name - "top", "bottom", "+x", "-x", "+y", "-y", a diagonal such as "-x+y", "slope" or "slope -x" - or a slot number as blocks lists it (for a cube: 0 top, 1 -x, 2 -y, 3 +x, 4 +y, 5 bottom; other shapes have their own slots, see blocks / shapes). The ground (z = 0) can be painted too.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `faces` | array of object | required | The faces to paint. |

## detail_faces

*act*

Put details (decals: windows, doors, signs...) on block faces, over their paint, laid out like paint_faces. Each: {"x", "y", "z", "face" (a direction name such as "+x" or a slot number, as paint_faces), "texture": a detail name from library(kind="details"), optional "u" / "v"}; "texture": "" removes the detail. To put a whole multi-face detail (e.g. 48 x 48 px = 3 x 3 faces) in one go use place_detail.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `faces` | array of object | required | The faces to decorate. |

## place_detail

*act*

Put a whole detail picture on a wall (or a roof) in one go, as the Architect's Apply Decal tool does: a detail W x H px covers W/16 x H/16 faces; the given face is its top-left corner as seen from outside, and it extends to the right along the wall and downwards (on a top face: towards -y and -x). E.g. a 48 x 48 px door on the +y wall with its top-left face at (16, 30, 3) covers x 16..14, z 3..1.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Cell x of the top-left face. |
| `y` | integer | required | Cell y. |
| `z` | integer | required | Cell z. |
| `face` | string | required | Wall direction "+x", "-x", "+y", "-y", or "top". |
| `detail` | string | required | Detail name (library kind=details, or one made with create_texture kind=detail). |

## paint_box

*act*

Paint the outside of the blocks in a box: every visible vertical face (diagonal ones too) gets the wall texture (and optionally a detail such as windows), every visible top and sloped roof face the roof texture - for any block shape, using the Architect's own visible-face bits.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x0` | integer | required | Box corner x. |
| `y0` | integer | required | Box corner y. |
| `z0` | integer | required | Box corner z. |
| `x1` | integer | required | Opposite corner x. |
| `y1` | integer | required | Opposite corner y. |
| `z1` | integer | required | Opposite corner z. |
| `walls` | string | `''` | Wall texture name (library kind=walls / colors / custom); empty to leave walls as they are. |
| `roof` | string | `''` | Roof texture name (library kind=roofs); empty to leave tops as they are. |
| `wall_detail` | string | `''` | Detail to put on the walls (library kind=details); empty for none. |

## place_props

*act*

Place props (trees, cars, benches, signs, rooftop units...) as the Architect's prop tool does: each {"prop": name from library(kind="props"), "x", "y" (the cell the prop is centred on), "z" (its bottom, default 1), "orientation": 0..3}. A prop fills its size in cells, which must be empty; placed_props lists the props on the building and remove_props takes them away.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `props` | array of object | required | The props to place. |

## placed_props

*read*

The props on the building being edited: prop name (as in library kind=props), orientation, the box of cells it fills (x0..x1, y0..y1, z0..z1) and its cell count.

No parameters.

## remove_props

*act*

Remove whole props: every prop that has a cell at one of the given positions (all its cells go).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | array of object | required | Positions {"x", "y"} or {"x", "y", "z"} (z omitted = any height), e.g. a prop's x0, y0 from placed_props. |

## copy_blocks

*act*

Copy (or move) everything in a box - blocks with their paint and details, and prop cells - by an offset, like the Architect's copy / cut / paste of a plane: e.g. copy floor 1 (z 1..1) up with dz=1 to add a storey, or repeat a bay of a facade along x. Undo takes the whole copy back.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x0` | integer | required | Box corner x. |
| `y0` | integer | required | Box corner y. |
| `z0` | integer | required | Box corner z. |
| `x1` | integer | required | Opposite corner x. |
| `y1` | integer | required | Opposite corner y. |
| `z1` | integer | required | Opposite corner z. |
| `dx` | integer | `0` | Offset in x. |
| `dy` | integer | `0` | Offset in y. |
| `dz` | integer | `0` | Offset in z. |
| `move` | boolean | `false` | Remove the originals (cut and paste). |
| `overwrite` | boolean | `false` | Replace blocks already in the target cells (otherwise the call is refused if any target cell is taken). |

## fill_paint

*act*

The Architect's Fill tool: paint (or put a detail on) the given face and every face connected to it that points the same way (shape and rotation included), can be seen and has the same paint (or detail) as that face - e.g. one whole wall, a whole flat roof, one side of a sloped roof, or the whole lot ground (z = 0, face "top"). Textures are laid out continuously as paint_faces does.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Cell x of the starting face. |
| `y` | integer | required | Cell y. |
| `z` | integer | required | Cell z (0 = ground). |
| `face` | string | required | Direction name ("top", "+x", "-y", "slope -x", ...) or a slot number as text ("3"), as paint_faces. |
| `texture` | string | required | Paint name (library walls / roofs / ground / colors / custom) or, with detail=true, a detail name; "" clears. |
| `detail` | boolean | `false` | Fill with a detail instead of paint. |

## rotate_building

*act*

Turn the building on its lot by quarter turns, as the Architect's Rotate button (Space) does. Every block moves with it: with N cells a side, one turn moves the block at (x, y) to (N-1-y, x), so coordinates change. This sets which side faces which way in SimCity. To only look at other sides use view_image(rotation=...) instead. Undo turns it back.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `turns` | integer | `1` | Quarter turns, 1..3 (negative turns the other way). |

## undo

*act*

Undo the last editing calls (place / fill / remove / paint / detail / props), one call per step, with the Architect's own undo records. History starts when the building is opened or created and ends at a render (render_building resets the Architect's undo log).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | integer | `1` | How many calls to undo. |

## redo

*act*

Redo calls undone with undo (until a new edit is made).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | integer | `1` | How many calls to redo. |

## view_image

*read*

The Building Architect's view of the building being edited, read from its own render buffer (no screenshot). construct = untextured blocks with the edit grid and side planes; paint / detail / props = the textured building (on the Architect's showcase lot at low zoom); file = its preview. To see other sides the building is turned with the Rotate button and turned back afterwards (coordinates and undo are unaffected).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `'paint'` | construct \| paint \| detail \| props \| file. |
| `zoom` | integer | `-1` | View zoom 0..5 (higher = closer; the program limits the range for each lot size); -1 keeps the current zoom. |
| `rotation` | integer | `0` | Quarter turns to view the building from, 0..3 (0 = as edited: the +x, +y sides face you; 2 = the back). |
| `all_sides` | boolean | `false` | Return all four sides in one picture (2 x 2: rotation 0 top left, 1 top right, 2 bottom left, 3 bottom right). |
| `crop` | boolean | `true` | Cut the picture down to the building (and whatever else is drawn around it). |

## render_building

*act*

Render a project with the Architect's own renderer into the sprites SimCity 3000 uses, and return how the building looks in the game (the four rotations side by side, decoded from the render output, no screenshot). By default the render goes to a temporary file; install=true adds the building to the game's Apps\BARender\BAT.DAT (keeping every other building; the old file is backed up next to it), as the Architect's render for SimCity does, so the game can use it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `''` | Project file name in the Buildings folder (with or without .bld) or a full path; empty = the building being edited (saved first with save_building). |
| `zoom` | integer | `4` | Zoom of the returned picture: 1 (8 px per tile) .. 5 (128 px per tile). |
| `install` | boolean | `false` | Also write the building into the game's BAT.DAT (SimCity 3000 must not be running: it keeps that file open). |

## photo_add

*set*

Add a photograph to work from (photo-to-building, no Building Architect needed): a picture file or base64, optionally cropped and scaled (coordinates in later calls are in the stored picture). Later calls refer to it by name; photo_view shows it with a pixel grid for reading coordinates.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | A short name for the photo (letters, digits, spaces, - and _). |
| `image_path` | string | `''` | A picture file (JPG, PNG...). |
| `image_base64` | string | `''` | Or the picture as base64 (or a data: URL). |
| `crop` | array of integer or null | `null` | [x0, y0, x1, y1] in the original picture's pixels to keep only the building. |
| `scale` | number | `1.0` | Resize after cropping (e.g. 0.5); about 30 - 60 px per metre of facade is plenty. |

## photo_view

*read*

A photo (or part of it) with a labelled pixel grid in the photo's own coordinates - for reading the corners of facades, roofs and windows to use in photo materials (quad).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | The photo's name (photo_add). |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | Left edge of the part to show (photo pixels). |
| `y0` | integer | `0` | Top edge. |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | Right edge (-1 = the photo's width). |
| `y1` | integer | `-1` | Bottom edge (-1 = the photo's height). |
| `grid` | integer | `0` | Grid spacing in photo pixels (0 = about 10 lines across the shown part). |

## photo_rectify

*read*

Preview a photo material: the region inside quad (four photo pixels: the facade's top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left corners, as photo_view shows them) with the perspective removed - what a face will be painted with. Give the face's real size to see it in proportion.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | The photo's name. |
| `quad` | array of array of number | required | [[x, y], [x, y], [x, y], [x, y]]: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. |
| `width_m` | number | `0` | The face's width in metres (0 = keep the photo's proportions). |
| `height_m` | number | `0` | The face's height in metres. |

## photo_model_render

*read*

Render a photo-built building model (see guide topic "photo": parts in metres, authored facade / pattern / texture / photo materials) exactly as SimCity 3000 will draw it - its projection, rotations, lot and lighting matched to the game's own buildings - without the Building Architect. Returns facts about the model and a picture (four rotations side by side, or one). Iterate until it matches the photo (compare them side by side, enlarged), then photo_model_export.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | object or null | `null` | The model object {"name", "lot", "materials": {...}, "parts": [...]}. |
| `model_path` | string | `''` | Or a JSON file holding the model. |
| `rotation` | integer | `-1` | 0..3, or -1 for all four. |
| `zoom` | integer | `5` | 1..5 (5 = 128 px per tile, the game's closest zoom, drawn at full resolution). |
| `shadows` | boolean | `true` | Cast soft shadows from the key light. |

## photo_model_export

*act*

Turn a photo-built model into a SimCity 3000 building: all 20 sprites (5 zooms x 4 rotations; zoom 5 at full resolution unless native_zoom5 is false) in the game's own format, written to a temporary DAT file; with install=true also into Apps\BARender\MCP Photo Buildings.DAT (our own file - the Architect's BAT.DAT is not touched; the previous file is backed up). The game reads that folder when it starts, so restart SimCity 3000, then put the building in a city with the game server's replace_building (it lists user-made buildings). Returns the building key and the zoom-5 picture.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model` | object or null | `null` | The model object. |
| `model_path` | string | `''` | Or a JSON file holding it. |
| `install` | boolean | `false` | Also add it to the game's user-building folder (SimCity 3000 must be restarted to see it). |
| `native_zoom5` | boolean | `true` | Store real 128 px-per-tile zoom-5 images (sharper) instead of zoom 4 doubled as the Architect does. |
| `architect` | string | `''` | Architect name stored with the building (default the model's "architect"). |
| `description` | string | `''` | Description (default the model's "description"). |

## photo_buildings

*read*

The photo-built buildings installed for the game (Apps\BARender\MCP Photo Buildings.DAT): name, building id, lot size, architect and description - what replace_building in the game server can show in a city after a restart.

No parameters.

## photo_building_remove

*destructive*

Take an installed photo-built building out of the game's user-building file (a test building, an old version): its records go, the other buildings stay, the previous file is kept as a dated .bak beside it. Like installing, it takes effect when SimCity 3000 next starts; first undo replace_building in any city that shows it.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | The building's name or id, as photo_buildings lists it. |

## bat_quit

*destructive*

Close the Building Architect (unsaved changes are lost).

No parameters.
